Fix an integer $d\ge1$, a gas constant $R>0$, an adiabatic exponent $\gamma>1$, a constant reference entropy $s_0\in\mathbb R$, shear viscosity $\mu>0$, bulk viscosity $\zeta\ge0$, and heat conductivity $\kappa>0$. Put $c_v=R/(\gamma-1)$. A conservative state is $U=(\rho,m,E)\in\mathbb R\times\mathbb R^d\times\mathbb R$. Its **admissible state set** is

$$\mathcal G=\left\{(\rho,m,E):\rho>0,\ E>\frac{|m|^2}{2\rho}\right\}.$$

For $U\in\mathcal G$, define the velocity $u=m/\rho$, internal-energy density $\varepsilon=E-|m|^2/(2\rho)$, pressure $p=(\gamma-1)\varepsilon$, temperature $T=p/(R\rho)$, specific entropy $s(U)=c_v\log(p/\rho^\gamma)+s_0$, and mathematical entropy $\eta(U)=-\rho s(U)$. The Euler flux in coordinate direction $j$ is

$$F_j(U)=\bigl(\rho u_j,\ m u_j+p e_j,\ (E+p)u_j\bigr),\qquad j=1,\ldots,d,$$

where $e_j$ is the $j$th standard basis vector of $\mathbb R^d$. The mathematical entropy flux is $q_j(U)=\eta(U)u_j$.

For a differentiable velocity field, write $D=\operatorname{sym}\nabla u$ with $D_{ab}=(\partial_bu_a+\partial_au_b)/2$, and $D^0=D-(\operatorname{tr}D/d)I$. The Newtonian stress and Fourier viscous flux are

$$\tau=2\mu D^0+\zeta(\operatorname{tr}D)I, \qquad F_j^{\mathrm{visc}}=\bigl(0,\tau_{j1},\ldots,\tau_{jd},\ u\cdot\tau_{j\cdot}+\kappa\partial_jT\bigr).$$

The **compressible Navier–Stokes–Fourier balance law** is the conservative system

$$\partial_tU+\sum_{j=1}^d\partial_jF_j(U) =\sum_{j=1}^d\partial_jF_j^{\mathrm{visc}}(U,\nabla u,\nabla T).$$

Unless a boundary is specified separately, a periodic solution means that all fields and fluxes are periodic in each spatial coordinate. The positive parameters and the inequalities defining $\mathcal G$ imply $p>0$ and $T>0$.

Let $U_0=(\rho_0,m_0,E_0)$ and $U_1=(\rho_1,m_1,E_1)$ lie in $\mathcal G$, and let $0\le t\le1$. Then $\rho_t=(1-t)\rho_0+t\rho_1>0$ and convexity from step 1.1 gives $g(\rho_t,m_t)\le(1-t)g(\rho_0,m_0)+tg(\rho_1,m_1)$. derivations.claim: Set $\varepsilon=E-|m|^2/(2\rho)$ and $u=m/\rho$. Rewriting the entropy gives $\eta=-c_v\rho\log((\gamma-1)\varepsilon)+c_v\gamma\rho\log\rho-s_0\rho$. For an increment $\delta U=(a,b,c)$, its first internal-energy variation is $\delta\varepsilon=c-u\cdot b+|u|^2a/2$, and its second directional variation is $D^2\varepsilon[\delta U,\delta U]=-|b-ua|^2/\rho$. The chain rule therefore yields $D^2\eta[\delta U,\delta U]=c_v\left(\frac{\gamma}{\rho}a^2-\frac{2}{\varepsilon}a\,\delta\varepsilon+\frac{\rho}{\varepsilon^2}(\delta\varepsilon)^2+\frac1{\varepsilon}|b-ua|^2\right)$. The first three terms have matrix $\begin{pmatrix}\gamma/\rho&-1/\varepsilon\\-1/\varepsilon&\rho/\varepsilon^2\end{pmatrix}$, whose leading diagonal entry is positive and determinant is $(\gamma-1)/\varepsilon^2>0$. The last term is nonnegative. If the full quadratic form is zero, then $a=\delta\varepsilon=0$ and $b=0$; the formula for $\delta\varepsilon$ then gives $c=0$. Thus the Hessian is positive definite.

Differentiating the same expression for $\eta$ gives $\beta=c_v\rho/\varepsilon=1/T$ and $v=(c_v\gamma-s-\beta|u|^2/2,\beta u,-\beta)$. Positive definiteness from step 1.1 makes $D_Uv=D_U^2\eta$ invertible, so the inverse function theorem gives a smooth local inverse near each state. Since $\mathcal G$ is convex by [F2], integrating the positive Hessian along the segment between any two distinct states also gives strict convexity of $\eta$ on $\mathcal G$.

Fix $j$ and an arbitrary variation $dU=(d\rho,dm,dE)$, and write $du_j=(dm_j-u_j\,d\rho)/\rho$. Differentiating the flux in [F1] gives $dF_j=(u_jd\rho+\rho du_j,\ u_jdm+m\,du_j+e_jdp,\ u_j(dE+dp)+(E+p)du_j)$. For two admissible states $U_L,U_R\in\mathcal G$, let $\bar U=(U_L+U_R)/2$, $\Delta v=v(U_R)-v(U_L)$, and $\Delta\psi_j=\psi_j(U_R)-\psi_j(U_L)$, where $v$ and $\psi_j$ are given by [[lem-compressible-ideal-gas-entropy-pair-and-variables]]. Define the symmetric two-point flux

$$F_j^{\mathrm{ec}}(U_L,U_R)= \begin{cases} F_j(U_L),&\Delta v=0,\\[2mm] F_j(\bar U)+\dfrac{\Delta\psi_j-\Delta v^TF_j(\bar U)}{\|\Delta v\|^2}\,\Delta v,&\Delta v\ne0. \end{cases}$$

The norm is Euclidean in the $d+2$ conservative-state coordinates. The convexity result [[lem-compressible-admissible-state-set-open-convex]] ensures $\bar U\in\mathcal G$.

For the ideal-gas model in [[def-compressible-navier-stokes-fourier-model]], the mathematical entropy $\eta=-\rho s$ has positive-definite Hessian on $\mathcal G$. Its entropy variables are

$$v(U)=\nabla_U\eta(U)=\left(c_v\gamma-s-\frac{\beta|u|^2}{2},\ \beta u,\ -\beta\right),\qquad \beta=\frac{c_v\rho}{\varepsilon}=\frac1T.$$

The Euler entropy flux $q_j(U)=\eta(U)u_j$ is compatible with $F_j$, meaning $\nabla_Uq_j=(\nabla_U\eta)^TDF_j$, and its entropy potential is $\psi_j(U)=v(U)^TF_j(U)-q_j(U)=\rho R u_j$. Consequently $U\mapsto v(U)$ is a local diffeomorphism at every $U\in\mathcal G$ and $\eta$ is strictly convex on $\mathcal G$.

The set $\mathcal G$ in [[def-compressible-navier-stokes-fourier-model]] is open and convex in $\mathbb R^{d+2}$. In particular, the arithmetic mean of any two admissible conservative states is admissible.

Hence $\Delta v\ne0$, so the denominator in [F1] is nonzero; also $\bar U\in\mathcal G$. This proves well-definedness and consistency.

Exchanging $U_L$ and $U_R$ leaves $\bar U$ fixed and changes the signs of both $\Delta v$ and $\Delta\psi_j$. Thus the scalar correction coefficient in [F1] changes sign while its vector factor changes sign, leaving the flux unchanged. The diagonal branch is also symmetric.

Fix a state $X\in\mathcal G$ and write $U_R=X+h/2$, $U_L=X-h/2$ for small $h$. The entropy compatibility in [F2] implies $D_U\psi_j(X)=F_j(X)^TD_Uv(X)$. Symmetric Taylor expansions therefore give $\Delta v=D_Uv(X)h+O(|h|^3)$ and $\Delta\psi_j=F_j(X)^TD_Uv(X)h+O(|h|^3)$, so $N:=\Delta\psi_j-\Delta v^TF_j(X)=O(|h|^3)$. Positive definiteness of $D_Uv(X)$ implies $|\Delta v|\ge c|h|$ in a sufficiently small neighborhood of $h=0$.

When $\Delta v\ne0$, dotting [F1] with $\Delta v$ cancels its denominator and gives $\Delta v^TF_j(\bar U)+\Delta\psi_j-\Delta v^TF_j(\bar U)=\Delta\psi_j$. When $\Delta v=0$, step 1.1 gives $U_L=U_R$, so both sides are zero.

On that neighborhood, the correction $N\Delta v/|\Delta v|^2$ is $O(|h|^2)$ and tends to zero on the diagonal. Differentiating the symmetric Taylor remainders gives $\partial_hN=O(|h|^2)$, $\partial_XN=O(|h|^3)$, $\partial_h\Delta v=O(1)$, and $\partial_X\Delta v=O(|h|)$. The quotient rule then shows that the correction derivatives are bounded and tend to zero as $h\to0$; its diagonal extension is $C^1$. Away from the diagonal the denominator is nonzero by step 1.1 and the formula is smooth. Thus the flux is locally Lipschitz everywhere on $\mathcal G\times\mathcal G$.

$$\mathcal G=\left\{(\rho,m,E):\rho>0,\ E>\frac{|m|^2}{2\rho}\right\}.$$

For $U\in\mathcal G$, define the velocity $u=m/\rho$, internal-energy density $\varepsilon=E-|m|^2/(2\rho)$, pressure $p=(\gamma-1)\varepsilon$, temperature $T=p/(R\rho)$, specific entropy $s(U)=c_v\log(p/\rho^\gamma)+s_0$, and mathematical entropy $\eta(U)=-\rho s(U)$. The Euler flux in coordinate direction $j$ is

$$F_j(U)=\bigl(\rho u_j,\ m u_j+p e_j,\ (E+p)u_j\bigr),\qquad j=1,\ldots,d,$$

where $e_j$ is the $j$th standard basis vector of $\mathbb R^d$. The mathematical entropy flux is $q_j(U)=\eta(U)u_j$.

For a differentiable velocity field, write $D=\operatorname{sym}\nabla u$ with $D_{ab}=(\partial_bu_a+\partial_au_b)/2$, and $D^0=D-(\operatorname{tr}D/d)I$. The Newtonian stress and Fourier viscous flux are

$$\partial_tU+\sum_{j=1}^d\partial_jF_j(U) =\sum_{j=1}^d\partial_jF_j^{\mathrm{visc}}(U,\nabla u,\nabla T).$$

Let $\mathcal I=\{1,\ldots,M\}$ be a nonempty finite periodic node set. Let $H\in\mathbb R^{M\times M}$ be diagonal with strictly positive entries, and for each direction $j=1,\ldots,d$ let $D_j\in\mathbb R^{M\times M}$ satisfy the periodic diagonal-norm SBP identities

$$HD_j+D_j^TH=0,\qquad D_j\mathbf1=0.$$

For a nodal array $w=(w_i)_{i\in\mathcal I}$, $D_jw$ means componentwise matrix multiplication, $(D_jw)_i=\sum_{\ell\in\mathcal I}(D_j)_{i\ell}w_\ell$. Given admissible nodal states $U_i\in\mathcal G$, write $v_i=v(U_i)$. Define the semidiscrete system

$$\dot U_i+2\sum_{j=1}^d\sum_{\ell\in\mathcal I}(D_j)_{i\ell}F_j^{\mathrm{ec}}(U_i,U_\ell) =\sum_{j,k=1}^d\left[D_j\left(\bigl(K_{jk}(U_i)(D_kv)_i\bigr)_{i\in\mathcal I}\right)\right]_i, \qquad i\in\mathcal I,$$

where $F_j^{\mathrm{ec}}$ is the two-point flux in [[def-ideal-gas-entropy-conservative-pair-flux]] and $K_{jk}$ is the viscous block matrix in [[lem-compressible-viscous-flux-entropy-variable-factorization]]. This definition specifies a periodic semidiscrete operator on $\mathcal G^M$; it does not include a time discretization or a positivity limiter.

The flux in [[def-ideal-gas-entropy-conservative-pair-flux]] is well-defined for every pair in $\mathcal G\times\mathcal G$, symmetric in its two states, and consistent in the sense that $F_j^{\mathrm{ec}}(U,U)=F_j(U)$. It satisfies

$$(v(U_R)-v(U_L))^TF_j^{\mathrm{ec}}(U_L,U_R)=\psi_j(U_R)-\psi_j(U_L).$$

The flux is locally Lipschitz on $\mathcal G\times\mathcal G$.

For $U\in\mathcal G$, let $Z=(Z_1,\ldots,Z_d)$ and $W=(W_1,\ldots,W_d)$ be arrays of entropy-variable gradients, with $Z_k,W_k\in\mathbb R^{d+2}$. Write $Z_{k,m_\ell}$ for the momentum-variable component and $Z_{k,E}$ for the energy-variable component. Define

$$G_{k\ell}(Z)=Z_{k,m_\ell}+u_\ell Z_{k,E},\qquad c_k(Z)=Z_{k,E},$$

and $G^0(Z)=\operatorname{sym}G(Z)-(\operatorname{tr}G(Z)/d)I$. Define the linear map

$$\mathcal R_U Z=\bigl(\sqrt{2\mu T}\,G^0(Z),\ \sqrt{\zeta T}\,\operatorname{tr}G(Z),\ \sqrt{\kappa}\,T c(Z)\bigr).$$

The bilinear form

$$\mathcal B_U(Z,W)=2\mu T\,G^0(Z):G^0(W)+\zeta T\,\operatorname{tr}G(Z)\operatorname{tr}G(W)+\kappa T^2\sum_{k=1}^d c_k(Z)c_k(W)$$

has the factorization $\mathcal B_U(Z,W)=(\mathcal R_UZ)\cdot(\mathcal R_UW)=\sum_{j,k}Z_j^TK_{jk}(U)W_k$, so $K(U)=\mathcal R_U^*\mathcal R_U$ is a symmetric positive-semidefinite block matrix.
